The test image shows a close-up of a surface covered in dense white/grayish-beige cottony mycelium with dark spots throughout. This looks like a fungal disease. The plant part appears to be a fruit (pod) or stem based on the curved surface.

Key candidates: **Rhizopus_Soft_Rots** (whitish-gray mycelia + black sporangia), **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (white cotton mycelium + sclerotia), **Gray_Mold**, **Southern_Blight**.

Now viewing reference images - one per class:

This Rhizopus seed reference (ID 5369124) is an near-identical match to the test image (ID 5369123) - same dense whitish-gray cottony mycelium with black sporangia scattered throughout. Continuing with other classes:

All 8 views used. Summary of findings:

- **Rhizopus_Soft_Rots/seed** (Bugwood_2, ID 5369124) = near-identical match to test image (ID 5369123) — same dense whitish-gray cottony mycelium covering the surface with dark black sporangia dots scattered throughout. Sequential Bugwood IDs suggest same photoshoot.
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot/stem** — bleached stem with embedded sclerotia, no dense mycelium mat
- **Gray_Mold/stem** — brown lesion, no cottony mass
- **Southern_Blight/stem** — tan/white tissue damage, no mycelial mat matching the test
- **Alternaria/stem** — dark stem canker at soil line, no mycelium
- **Anthracnose/pod** — dark sunken fruit rot, no mycelium

The test image shows dense whitish-gray fibrous mycelium with numerous dark spherical sporangia — the classic macroscopic appearance of **Rhizopus Soft Rots**. The visual match to the seed reference is definitive.
